summary: Halyard-paper mutual NDA where the Dutch counterparty has widened the Purpose and use right, narrowed the carve-outs (deleting independent development), added a 24-month non-solicit, and commented asking for 18-month survival and Dutch law.

findings.quote: VLIET & VAN DER BERG ADVIES B.V., a private company with limited liability
findings.why: The counterparty entity details have been filled in (RQ07 correction); the lawyer should confirm them against the Dutch Trade Register.

findings.quote: each Party may disclose certain Confidential Information to the other Party
findings.why: The agreement is genuinely mutual: Disclosing Party and Receiving Party are defined by role so either party can be either.

findings.quote: potential commercial opportunities, strategic evaluations, advisory engagements, and any other internal or external business activities of the respective Parties from time to time
findings.why: The Purpose is widened to any internal or external business activities, so it is no longer limited to discussions about a potential commercial relationship.
findings.draft_redline: The Parties wish to enter into discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship between them (the Purpose).
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have kept the Purpose to discussions about a potential commercial relationship between us, as the broader wording would let confidential information be used well beyond those discussions. We are happy to name a specific project if that helps.

findings.quote: or for its internal business assessment, service benchmarking and market evaluation
findings.why: The insertion permits use for the Receiving Party's own business assessment, benchmarking and market evaluation, which goes beyond use solely for the Purpose.
findings.draft_redline: 2.1.2 not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose;
findings.note_to_counterparty: We need to keep use of confidential information limited solely to the Purpose, so we have restored that wording and removed the additional internal-use rights.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: The definition is mutual, tied to the Purpose, covers marked or reasonably confidential information and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: any groepsmaatschappij within the meaning of Article 2:24b of the Dutch Civil Code
findings.why: A Dutch-law group concept is added to the Group definition for the Counterparty only, which may widen who counts as a Group member beyond the Companies Act 2006 test; a lawyer should check.
findings.draft_redline: Delete the insertion in clause 1.1.5; clause 4 already permits disclosure to Group members on a need-to-know basis.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Clause 4 already permits disclosure to your Group members on a need-to-know basis, so we do not think the additional Dutch-law definition is needed.

findings.quote: [[DEL: written records or other reasonable]][[INS: contemporaneous documentary]] evidence
findings.why: The evidence standard is raised from written records or other reasonable evidence to contemporaneous documentary evidence, which narrows all the carve-outs.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1 The obligations set out in Clause 2 shall not apply to any information which the Receiving Party can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence:
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have kept the standard of proof as written records or other reasonable evidence, which is workable for both parties.

findings.quote: as evidenced by the Receiving Party's written records dated prior to the date of this Agreement
findings.why: The already-held carve-out is narrowed so it only applies if evidenced by written records dated before the Agreement.
findings.draft_redline: 3.1.2 was already lawfully in the possession of the Receiving Party prior to its disclosure by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party, free from any restriction as to its use or disclosure;
findings.note_to_counterparty: The general evidence standard in clause 3.1 already covers this point, so we have removed the extra dated-records requirement.

findings.quote: [[DEL: 3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.]]
findings.why: The independent development carve-out is deleted, so one of the four required carve-outs is missing.
findings.draft_redline:
3.1.3 is lawfully received by the Receiving Party after the date of this Agreement from an independent third party who is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of that information; or
3.1.4 is independently developed by or on behalf of the Receiving Party without access to, use of, or reference to any of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We have reinstated the independent development exception, as it is a standard protection that benefits both parties.

findings.quote: may disclose the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information to those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives and Group members is allowed on a need-to-know basis and the Receiving Party stays liable for them under 4.1.3.

findings.quote: take all reasonable steps requested by the Disclosing Party (at the Disclosing Party's cost) to resist or narrow the scope of the required disclosure
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Ten Business Days, officer-signed confirmation and a backup and legal-retention exception in 6.2 with continuing confidentiality in 6.3 all match the preferred position.

findings.quote: other than the limited right to use the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose in accordance with the terms of this Agreement
findings.why: Clause 7.1 keeps all Confidential Information and IP with the Disclosing Party and 7.2 grants no licence beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "as is" basis.
findings.why: Information is provided as is with no warranty from either Party, as in the preferred position.

findings.quote: nothing in this Agreement shall operate or be construed so as to exclude, restrict or limit the liability of either Party in respect of fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation
findings.why: The rewrite is wordier but the substance is the same: a mutual reliance disclaimer with the fraud carve-out retained.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: to enter into any further agreement or transaction with the other Party, or to proceed with the Purpose or any commercial relationship
findings.why: Mutual no-obligation-to-proceed wording is included.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: A mutual publicity restriction requires prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Only business contact details are expected and any other personal data needs a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first; the added EU GDPR reference does not change this.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party
findings.why: A two-year term with 30 days' notice to terminate early matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination
findings.why: Three-year survival with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets is the preferred position.

findings.quote: Our internal policy caps post-termination confidentiality obligations at 18 months from the date of disclosure.
findings.why: The comment asks for survival of 18 months from disclosure, which is under the 2-year minimum and would also cut Trade Secret protection; RQ01 says to escalate below 2 years.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We can offer to shorten survival to two years after expiry or termination, with continued protection for Trade Secrets for as long as they remain Trade Secrets, but we are unable to go below that.

findings.quote: any director, officer, partner, consultant, software engineer or senior employee of a Party or any member of its Group with whom the other Party or any member of its Group comes into contact
findings.why: The new Key Personnel definition supports the non-solicit and extends to consultants and any Group personnel encountered, so it is not limited to staff worked with in the discussions.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We do not include non-solicitation terms in our NDA, so the Key Personnel definition is not needed and we have removed it.

findings.quote: neither Party shall, and each Party shall procure that no member of its Group shall, without the prior written consent of the other Party, directly or indirectly solicit, entice away, offer employment to, engage or employ any Key Personnel
findings.why: The new non-solicit runs for the term plus 24 months, which is over 12 months, has no general-advertising exception, and covers hiring of broad Key Personnel across the Group.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Our standard NDA does not contain a non-solicitation covenant, and the proposed one is longer and broader than we can accept for a confidentiality agreement. We have therefore removed it.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek injunctive and equitable relief, with remedies cumulative under 11.2.

findings.quote: without the prior written consent of the other Party
findings.why: Neither Party may assign or deal with its rights without prior written consent.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure
findings.why: A reverse engineering prohibition is retained.

findings.quote: shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales
findings.why: The operative text keeps English law; the counterparty's request for a change is in the margin comment.

findings.quote: our standard position is for Dutch law and the District Court of Amsterdam (Rechtbank Amsterdam) to apply under Clauses 12.10 and 12.11
findings.why: The comment asks for Dutch law and Amsterdam courts, which is another governing law and a jurisdiction outside England and Wales; RQ03 says decline and offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction.
findings.draft_redline: Keep clauses 12.10 and 12.11 as drafted (English law, exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales); fallback: English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to move away from English law, as it is our standard position across all of our agreements. If it would help, we could consider making the English courts' jurisdiction non-exclusive.

findings.quote: the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: Exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales is the preferred position and is unchanged.
